Kids First Big & Fun Microscope Science Experiment Kit | Easy-to-Use Kids Microscope | Ages 4-6 | STEM Experiment Guide and Full-Color User Manual | 72 Images | Extra-wide Eyepiec with Light-up Stage I was disappointed in this microscope, BUT it is for preschoolers. Each part was designed with them in mind. It doesn't magnify much, but it's for the benefit of their eyes. It's also designed so that they don't have to shut one eye to see. It's simple! If you're looking for something more advanced, you'll most definitely want to go another route. This one is more of a toy than a microscope.

It comes with 24 slides, with 3 items on each one. (Plus one blank one.) There's an included book that tells what it is on each of the slides(page 27 and 28). There's no storage for these at all. It would have been nice for a container or bag of some sort to be included to hold all of these. For now, we have the microscope and the slides within a basket, and that makes it easy to pull it off the shelf.

To use the light part of the microscope, you have to put in 2 AAA batteries, which are not included. Flip the switch and a light will come on. Just place a slide under the lens. (It will only go one way.) There's a knob that turns on the front, and this will move the slide back and forth. That's it. There's no way to zoom in and out.

I wouldn't recommend this microscope unless you want it as the most basic introduction to very young children(5ish and under). Even then if they've already been introduced to a microscope, they'll probably be disappointed in this one.
text_fidelity_b: Kids First Big & Fun Microscope Science Experiment Kit | Easy-to-Use Kids Microscope | Ages 4-6 | STEM Experiment Guide and Full-Color User Manual | 72 Images | Extra-wide Eyepiec with Light-up Stage

LEGO Creator Expert Vestas Wind Turbine 10268 Building Kit (826 Pieces) This LEGO CREATOR EXPERT VESTAS WIND TURBINE BUILDING KIT (10268; 826 Piece) is a fascinating set that’s much more fun than the advertising makes it appear. Its best feature is also its greatest drawback--the huge turbine blades take a lot of space to display and operate. The blades are motorized (with a servo hidden in the “Vestas” box at the top), and when they’re turning, the two house entrance lights turn on. What better way to dramatize the point that a single huge wind turbine can power thousands of homes?

The model is slightly challenging to build, because it calls for a lot of studs-not-on-top assembly. It’s especially interesting to see how the heavy wind turbine assemblage is secured to the base with only LEGO elements. The set does use specialized large green elements around the shaft to hide the battery box and to help hold the wind turbine firmly.

The model also demonstrates the one feature that bothers me about wind turbines as a source of electricity--they are huge, and loom over their surrounding landscape. The little house is dwarfed by the wind turbine. The house is cute, with windows and door that open, a range and sink, a lamp on a table, and a patio with a table and chairs (created from “repurposed” wheel-well elements).

The minifigs (two Vestas engineers, a female homeowner, and a dog) are great. The engineers have a van that holds their work bench and a hand truck loaded with service tanks and a big assortment of tools. The instruction book includes several pages describing the development of wind turbines as a power source, and showing diagrams of how they work to create electricity from wind currents.

The wind turbine on the model can be rotated by hand atop the shaft. Only the wind turbine blades are motorized. The blades are operated by a switch at the bottom of the shaft. The motor and lights run on 6 AA batteries (not included). The trees in the set are made from plants. (My LEGO Wind Turbine set was purchased from a LEGO Shop.)
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert Vestas Wind Turbine 10268 Building Kit (826 Pieces)

THE GOOD:
🌵 The sets are individually packaged, with their own directions, pieces, and coffee cup container. The box has a picture of the set inside, so if you wanted, you could give a set as a gift. Or if there’s a certain succulent you want to build, you can easily find it.

🌵 The sets are quick builds. It took me about 75 minutes to do all 12.

🌵 The instructions are simple, there are a few confusing steps but since these are plants, I was okay with them not being perfect.

🌵 The finished succulents do make cool display pieces, and are a perfect size for desks, bookshelves, or even windowsills. They are small: about 2 inches at the widest point and 5 inches for the tallest.

THE BAD:
🌵 The pieces don’t stay together very well. Some do and some do not. I had several construction accidents while building because some pieces clicked and some did not. Some pieces are very loose, one of the succulents (February, Plum Blossom) fell apart while I was building another.

🌵 I was unable to build one of the succulents because the thing would just not stay together. That was the December set, Antirrhinum majus. The main body of the plant is two pieces that will not snap together.

🌵 My sunflower is missing a petal because the necessary piece was malformed.

🌵 The coffee cup lids are a cute idea, but they did not stay connected to the cups. The lids are intended as the base for each cup, but no matter how hard I tried, the cups popped right off the lids. Fortunately, the cups are stable without needing to sit on the lids.

Overall, while this box of 12 succulents is a good value, I was somewhat disappointed that the succulents didn’t always stay together. A finished set shouldn’t fall apart while it’s sitting on the table because the pieces are loose.

text_fidelity_a:
Evviva Ant Habitat W/LED Light. Enjoy A Magnificent Habitat. Great for Kids & Adults. Evviva Ant Ecosystem W/Enhanced Blue Gel. Educational & Learning Science Kit. Live Ants Not Included This ant farm was a fascinating gift for everyone, not just the 6 year old who got it. We ordered the ants from AntsAlive .com and when they arrived they quickly scurried about, digging their first hole within a few hours. Before you add the ants, you must poke 3 to 4 holes in the gel to help the ants get started. I’m wondering if the negative reviews forgot this step, leaving the ants confused in the farm on where they could go.

I highly recommend refrigerating the ants for 10 minutes before you add them to the farm so they don’t immediately escape. I also highly recommend putting them in on the side nearest the white air hole plug. Inevitably a few ants will have died in shipment and it’s much easier to remove them through the hole then removing the entire lid (as others will try to escape).

Why this ant farm is better than others?
1) The ants food and water supply is in the gel. Other ant farms require food and water be added for the ants; adding too much can create mold or too little and the ants are hungry. It’s challenging to calculate and extra work.

2) The glass is fairly narrow front to back so it’s likely the ants (as they did for us) will dig right to the class so you can see them clearly while they work under ground.

3) The light and magnifying glass make it very easy to see every ant at work.

4) The farm is reusable. You can clean out the old gel and ants and buy new ants and gel for a second use.

I highly recommend this gift for any child aged 4-10. Certainly older children and adults will enjoy it too.

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos A Column of Fire: The Game When I first asked my family if I should get this game, they were not quite sure what to think. We went and looked at a bunch of videos and it looked really good. So, I ordered it. Then I watched a few more videos and wondered.. did I make a mistake?

WHAT IS THIS GAME LIKE?
This game is based upon a book. I have not read the book so if you are concerned that might affect your like of this game, keep in mind that I had no idea about this series of books, so it did not affect game play for me.

The game comes with a board that folds into a fourth of its size- a real plus for storage. It has a plastic storage area which holds all of the pieces- and yes, there are pieces. You press out the cardboard pieces so that you can keep them to play the game in the future. It is not hard to do and they pressed out cleanly.

There are cards and several sets of dice. Each player gets a set of dice. Maximum players are four. You can play successfully with two players.

HOW IS THE GAME TO LEARN?
I have to admit when we got the game, I was overtired, and very frustrated as it was. When one of our kids wanted to play, I was so afraid that I made a mistake and would hate this game. It really overwhelmed me. I could not make heads or tails of the instructions, and when trying to watch videos, well ,I was SURE I made a mistake in choosing this game.

Finally our child said, "How about we just try to play and walk through it?" I was not in the mood, but knew I had to test this out.

So... out came the very detailed instruction booklet. The beginning to set it up did not take too long, but it was not starting to make sense yet. I was not thrilled. Then as we read each move and worked through it, I was having a headache.

I kept with it, and about a half hour into the game, suddenly it all began to make sense. Then suddenly, I was enjoying it. In fact, I could not wait to play it again!

WHO MIGHT LIKE THIS GAME?
My kids who liked this were early teens and above range. It is really beautifully rendered, the cards and pieces are interesting, and the board itself is really nice to look at. It needs to be played at a nice table with room on it- like you might use for Monopoly or Life.

I would say that anyone who enjoys history, games that have purpose, and home educators might enjoy playing this game. It is not boring, nor is it a thrill ride, but it is a nice entertaining game that is interesting and did keep my attention.

If someone has an overabundance of energy and can not sit still unless entertained by a screen in constant motion, this might not work out for them. If someone has patience and enjoys artworks and interesting things (like playing with Legos or other similar things) this might be a game to try out for them.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Despite being a bit overwhelmed at first, once we plunged into the game, after a little while, I found it fun, interesting to play and found myself looking forward to playing it over again which is the same sentiment from the rest of the family as they have played it too.

MY RATING
Five stars for this. If you watch videos, don't get too overwhelmed, just plunge in and play it as a learning experience and it will suddenly click and off you go. I have to say it is one of the limited number of board games that make me want to play again and I look forward to it.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos A Column of Fire: The Game

text_fidelity_a:
Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games From the first time I saw Fallout the board game on the shelf I knew I wanted it. I have been a fan of the Fallout line since the first game. I have play almost every Fallout video game to come out and it was time to get the board game. After watching a couple videos on how to play, I was very intimidated. There seemed to be a lot of moving parts, card decks and miniatures. My fiancé and I play a most of our games together and I was thinking this would be one that would be a little out of her comfort zone.

I played through the single player game mode and enjoyed the game from the start. After the first game I knew the game was not as complicated as I thought. The game was so fun I stayed up till 3 am playing the game another 2 times. The next day I set it up for my fiancé and I, and I wasn’t disappointed. My favorite part of the game is the questing. The flavor and the ways you go about completing the quest feel like playing a video game. This is the closet I have come, in a board game, to a video game RPG. With hundreds of quest cards, the game replay is awesome. We both enjoyed the game and can’t wait to introduce it to our play group.

I play a lot of tabletop games with miniature and the piece in Fallout are top quality. Before long they will be painted and looking great on the great design of the game tiles. It really feels like you are in the wastelands. For those of you that have played the games, look forward to the quest for the Wasteland Survival Guide! All of the cards are well designed and I really like the decks are different physical sizes. There wasn’t enough room in the box for the insert and all the cards/game pieces. And there was not enough bags for all the game pieces, packaging could have been thought out a little more. Other than that, the game is great and I am looking forward to the expansion.
text_fidelity_b: Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

text_fidelity_a:
Treasure X King's Gold Treasure Tomb We have had a few other Treasure X sets in the past and my son really enjoyed them, with the sets keeping him busy for hours at a time carving and opening little slime filled packages with interesting toys inside. He has a castle "dollhouse" that he uses a lot of these toys in to create stories.

This treasure tomb was completely different in the sense that we work carving the toys out of chunks of sand this time, rather discovering each element and kind of figuring out everything as a puzzle.

The one criticism I have is that while I would've loved to have set this down and let my son just figure it out, the texture of a few of the things that you were supposed to just pick apart and peel away were not necessarily obvious that they were disposable elements of the toy, so the instruction manual was necessary, and because the instruction manual was not made big and pictorial, I had to sit there while they figured the whole thing out. My six-year-old figured out and understood most of it, but again, the parts that were not obvious that he was allowed to just tear into them really did need my reading the instructions and giving encouragement.

Aside from that minor quibble, this thing kept both my six-year-old and my three and half-year-old busy for a really long time. Hours. I sat them outside on the patio with a big pan to hold any messy elements, and they carved and drove swords into holes and put the keys in and popped everything out and overall had a ridiculously fun time.

The weird textural blue rock like slime in two of the tombs was particularly compelling to my son, who played with this stuff for about 45 minutes. I would've appreciated if the two tombs had had different types of slime or even just different colors, but my son had no such complaint and played for a long time.

While the tomb itself has not continued to hold their interest after about a week of play, some of the parts have been incorporated into frequent play with their castle dollhouse, and so overall even though part of it feels somewhat disposable, the other parts of it feel really fun for incorporating into our normal imaginative play.

This would make a fantastic birthday gift, because it is extremely flashy, tons of fun, lots of excited commentary and wowed children, and then lots of little toys that feel very fun and abundant.

Would I buy a set like this again? Very possibly, for a holiday or other occasion that I really want to feel super special and fancy. If there was a holiday where we were unable to have family and friends visit us or something like that, this set would bridge the gap to make the day feel sparkly and exciting for the kids.
text_fidelity_b: Treasure X King's Gold Treasure Tomb

Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over This game is best for really young children! I'd say 2-4. My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.

Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder These products, both the dry float lounger and the socializer are prime examples of why I test products the way I do prior to writing my review.

When I initially received these products and inflated them I was fairly impressed with the design and comfort - by 18 days later both were flat lumps of rubber in the trash.

First the socializer never held air. After inflation by the following morning it had deflated to around 70% capacity. I put it under water in the pool and discovered multiple small defects in 2 seams.

The dry float lounger lasted a bit longer at 18 days but then was found flat due to a separation at the seam.

It is important to note neither of these were ever used by children or in any rough play as when I review products I adhere to strict guidelines - and there are no children in the home.

While the socializer is listed as a dry float it appears the user’s calves and feet would be in the water. The lounger pool float is perfect for those who prefer to float completely out of the water. When floating on this no part of the body is submerged in the water.

While 88-90% of the world’s population is right handed this manufacturer chose to place the cup holder on the left side and made it too small to hold a standard 12 Oz can for both of these floats. This is simply poor designing.

While these floats come with a small patch kit, these are only helpful when repairing a puncture and absolutely will not hold a torn seam.

While these floats appeared to have promise initially, in well under a month they proved to be poorly designed, and of substandard construction and materials.

I would not recommend either of these products.
text_fidelity_b: Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder

Glitter Girls - Convertible Car for 14-inch Dolls - Toys, Clothes & Accessories for Girls 3-Year-Old & Up, Blue, Orange, Pink This convertible car for 14 inch dolls is completely awesome. We have a number of glitter girls dolls and two of them can fit into this convertible with ease, along with one of the glitter girls puppies sitting on a lap.

My kids saw this in a Christmas catalog and were completely enchanted with it, asking for it over and over again. It's about as big as you would expect given that the glitter girls both have to fit in there, and it has a dashboard that opens, a little side container that opens in between the two seats, two cupholders, and the trunk.

We have the glitter girls sweetshop and the accessories sweetshop that has some delightful cups of confectionery beverage, and I was delighted to find that these sweetshop beverages fit into the cupholders perfectly. (They also fit into the girls hands). The dashboard has very little room to put things in when it's open, and the angle is such that things really don't stay put very well at the dashboard is open, so I would've liked a little bit better design on that, because my kids had to work hard to find something they wanted to bring along that was small enough to fit. Same thing with the little container in between the two seats, if that could have been just a little bit wider, it would get used even more.

The trunk is also a little small and again the shape of the interior of it makes it harder for things to fit in, because it is just a rectangular box opening that is kind of slick, so when you put things in the kind of want to slide out. There is enough room in the car to where they could have made the trunk much more substantial, and it would've made this an even cooler car.

That said, these are just quibbles and the real proof of whether a toy is any good is in the pudding. My kids love it, and they've been playing with it nonstop and vrooming the girls around on all kinds of adventures since the car arrived. I've been delighted to see the amount of imaginative play that has taken place with the addition of a car, to where the girls can leave the bedroom and go on all kinds of fun adventures.

The car seems well-made and is very sturdy, the doors open, and if you need to put the windshield down for storage, it does fold down. Overall this is a great toy if you have 14 inch dolls who need some adventure in their lives.

Melissa & Doug Children's Book - Poke-a-Dot: What’s Your Favorite Color (Board Book with Buttons to Pop) - Poke A Dot /Push Pop Book For Toddlers And Kids Ages 3+ Let me begin by saying I’m a retired early childhood teacher of 24 years and was always in search of books that were appealing to children and encouraged them to engage in the books. This book would be at the top of my list of desirable books for children approximately 1-3 years of age. The book has visual and tactile appeal with a predictable rhyming text to promote early literacy! Love the vivid colors on each page to encourage children to learn their basic color names. As a bonus children are encouraged to tap the patented “pop-a-tropic” buttons to achieve the ever popular “bubble wrap” popping sound as they count the creatures on each page.

The book is impressive in that it is SO durable, with thick sturdy pages and a great binding, along with quality buttons! It can withstand the unintentional abuse that young children have been known to inflict on popular books!

To summarize, this book is well worth the purchase! text_fidelity_a:
Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot This is video pinball as it used to be, before today's highly sophisticated physics simulators: floaty ball mechanics, dumbed down special features, bizarre flipper behavior, etc. Which is what I expected.

But I have to say, I'm impressed at the care they put into it nevertheless. They carefully reproduced the major playfield features and loops, the special modes, the multiballs, the spinning pizza. They made the marquee its whole own separate screen so they could have the interactive elements. They have a clever alternative for the plunger (hold down the button for longer to shoot harder). The flipper buttons on the side can get a little finger-cramping, so they put duplicates on the back of the unit so you can hold the whole unit. And, for better or for worse, they reproduced all of the boys' voices. Ugh. And unless I'm mistaken, unlike most of the Tiny Arcade series, it actually saves your high scores.

It's not all good - the "Start Game"/"Game Over" text is hilariously blocky, like an Atari 2600 game, and it pops up on the playfield. I don't know why they didn't put it on the marquee LCD where it belonged. The ball vibrates weirdly on the habitrails. A couple times, particularly in multiball, I've had the ball just simply fall through the hinge of the flipper. But these aren't huge concerns, and they're easily laughed off.

One warning for sensitive and/or young users: I've always thought the original pinball game's marquee's presentation of April was excessively sexy (she's a hero in her own right, not eye candy, darn it) but in the cut down version it looks like... uh, something else entirely.

All in all, this way exceeded my expectations. And it's actually quite fun! I'm not interested in the other "boardwalk arcade" games so far, but I'd gladly buy more pinball games like this one if they're at a similar level of playability.
text_fidelity_b: Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot

Bugs in the Kitchen - Children's Board Game, Standard, 6 - 15 years My boys have had tons of fun with this game. I like it, too.

The set up is super easy, as well as playing the game. You basically put a thick cardboard piece in place, and a couple of tubes, and you're all set. It also comes with a hexbug and 12 various colored (non-moving)bugs. Each player will get 3 of those, and the goal is to get all 3 bugs to the other side first. The hexbug moves around under the board, through the tubes, and on the playing board. While he's on the playing board, you have to stop playing, and hope that he doesn't knock your bug out of place. If he does knock your bug completely off its spot, it has to go back to the beginning(after he's went off the upper board).

The only negative is the fact that the hexbug uses a button cell battery. We don't keep those things around typically, so in order to keep this game going, we'll now have to. It's still a very fun and easy game, though.

It's labeled for 6 and up, but my 3 and 5 year old children have loved it, too, along with my 8 year old. I'm guessing the 6 and up is due to a possible choking hazard, because it's a simple game to play.

Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange This is a simple "flick-and-write" game with good production values, a questionable rulebook, simple and fast gameplay, and a box that is just ridiculously large for what it is.

Gameplay is fast and straightforward, involving a Crokinole style mechanism for shooting your disc into a recessed game board with a central hole in the middle. This board has a plastic shelf with corner sections for "shooting" pieces, and they'll fall into a central area divided into four main sections. My central board easily comes loose from the shelving piece, and needs to be adjusted prior to gameplay almost all the time. Once you shoot, you'll be making marks onto your player board with the included markers, which are of average quality for a game like this. The boards are easily erasable - a major plus to the production aspect of the game.

The rules are not that hard, but they are explained in a way that makes learning the game quite a bit more difficult than it needs to be. Few examples are covered, and there will be a number of times that you run into situations where you aren't sure how to interpret the rule as written. Once you get it though, play is not too hard, and Sonora is something you can play with the kids after you've worked out the kinks. And they'll want to play this - it's colorful, with kid-friendly artwork, and the gameplay looks like a kid's game, but has enough meat to interest an adult for at least a little while. I don't know that I'd play this game too often, but it is certainly different and a good family game that will keep kids interested. You can play a few games back to back, as they'll run 20 minutes or so once you know the general flow of the game. For a family game night, this will be a good alternative to a more traditional strategy or roll-and-move board game.

The biggest downfall of this one is that the box is so large. As a gamer with a large collection, it's disappointing to see a 12x12 "Ticket to Ride" sized box for a game that could have opted for a foldable game board and fit into a very small game box. They would have lost nothing in doing this, and in fact, they might have fixed the issue I have with the main board. Even if they must have a one-piece board, dropping the molded plastic insert that holds a handful of discs and pens could have reduced the size by a few inches in depth. In reality, there's not much here in the box, and the components can be entirely stored in the recessed game board area alone. That would be about 3/4" in depth, not 3".

All in all, it's OK.
text_fidelity_b: Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange

Hot Wheels Set of 20 Toy Cars & Trucks in 1:64 Scale, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 50 cars is too much at once.

Days as a five year old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 50 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 50 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels Basic Car 50-Pack."

Anthony Trendl
treefortbooks.com

Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

With the motorcycle it offers a lot of play-ability. The figure fits the bike very well & can be posed in many ways on the bike. There are several pegs on the bike that fit into holes in Duke's boots to make him at least look balanced. Duke's helmet doesn't come off.
The stunt cycle's performance is also faithful to the movie which is unfortunate. The launcher is more of a gimmick & isn't necessary to use the toy. All of the cycle's motivation comes from winding a spring inside the bike by rolling it backwards. It's actually hard to put the bike in the launcher after it is wound without releasing the stored energy.
The motorcycle isn't quite as detailed or faithful to the movie but it looks great & it can take a beating without breaking. The cycle also has an extendable stand & set of dolly wheels that allows it to emulate a wheel stand while either rolling or just posing.
I wasn't able to get this to any kids before the review but I think it will be fun as a standalone or addition to other Toy Story character dolls. I can't think of any other full size dolls from the franchise that come with a vehicle.

text_fidelity_a: Mega Construx Call of Duty Heavy Tactical Cargo Truck The instructions were pretty clear. I only found one error, on a step where they ask you to find two of each brick, but only have and need one of each. The design almost works, but in the final assembly steps, I found the whole thing started to come apart around the middle of the undercarriage. It's a pretty common problem, but much worse than usual. I think part of it is that the front of the truck is built to flip up to expose the engine, and it just doesn't leave enough structural stability in the surrounding bricks. Upon completion, I immediately took it all apart and built a nice little hinged treasure box that looks like it is made of some kind of stone inlay with petrified wood interior. That's the beauty of this kind of toy. Not just that it can be mixed into the ol' brick box for future creations, but also that a set like this provides a lot of parts that are already designed into a pleasing color scheme.

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset There's a lot to love about sets like this that can be combined with other sets and used in creative ways. However, I'll say right up front that the whole point of getting this one is that you get the power booster, and the power booster, in my view, could use a big overhaul in the design.

Is it fun? Yes, without a doubt, the power booster is pretty fun. The problem? First of all, it takes 4 D batteries. Who uses D batteries nowadays? I'm lucky that we had just the right number of D battery adapters that allow us to use AA batteries instead, because otherwise I would have been in for a trip to the grocery store and I don't think it would've come cheap. What a power hog!

Second, the battery area needs to be taken apart with a screwdriver. This is fine for toys meant for the under three crowd, but for kids old enough to use a hot wheels set, it seems a little excessive and pretty irritating that every time a new set of batteries I need to become Mr. fix it and get out a screwdriver.

Third, when you actually go to play with it, the power booster is either on or off. So when the kid forgets about the hot wheels set and wanders off to go do something else, it's still sitting there using up your expensive D cell batteries. It's also noisy. I would've much preferred a button on the top that is easy for children to press that makes it work for a short period of time, such as 30 seconds. I'm guessing it is too much to ask to have a motion sensor turn it on or off or anything like that, so a limited time button that the child can find easily and press in the midst of gameplay without turning the power booster upside down would have been ideal.

That said, I think my primary criteria for evaluating hot wheels set is whether it is fun. Not fun for me, but fun for my kids. With only a little bit of help getting things set up, my three-year-old has been playing with this vigorously for two days and shows no signs of getting bored with it. We actually have a manual hot wheels ejecter to where you pull the lever back and press a button to make the car go really fast, and instead of using the power booster, we set that up for him to play with it on his own. The power booster is fun for when you make a big elaborate set up and are playing with a group of kids or with a parent for an extended period of time but to be honest I think when the batteries run down we may not replace them until there is a compelling reason to do so. It's just too noisy, and requires too much intervention from the parent to turn it on and off when it is needed and not just leave it noisily running and eating up our batteries.

The loop the loop works great with either the power booster or the manual ejection thing we already owned, and the tracks of course work with all of our other hot wheels sets.

I would probably recommend this most for people who have multiple children who will be playing with large and extended sets of hot wheels for 30 minutes or longer at a stretch. Otherwise, the power booster seems silly and kind of a waste.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome This is a fun ride-on toy for kids. I like that it sits close to the ground, which makes it better for younger kids, but the design is still “cool” enough that older kids will still like it. The dune buggy has a lot of good features. First, the blue color will appeal to both girls and boys. The vehicle has two speeds, which is nice. However, the parent lock-out needs to be removed to access the higher speed. The lock-out is a screw that’s fairly difficult to remove because of its location. The higher speed is definitely needed to easily ride in the wet grass, even on flat ground. It’s fairly easy to steer the vehicle and is a lot of fun for kids to drive.

To stop the vehicle, take your foot off the gas pedal. It will still slide a little on pavement, possibly because of the plastic wheels. It also will continue to slowly roll going downhill, even on a small incline. That’s why even though the guidelines say ages 3 to 7, I would use caution for younger kids unless you have a large, flat area with no nearby hills. Older kids, up to 11 or 12, will like it, too. However, with the position of the steering wheel, their height will determine how well they’ll comfortably fit in the dune buggy and be able to easily steer.

Be sure to charge the battery the night before using the first time. The battery only lasted about 15 minutes right out of the box after being putting the car together. I also learned the hard way that the dune buggy is heavy to push if it does bog down or if the battery dies. (The battery is rechargeable battery, but there isn’t a battery indicator, so I wasn’t expecting it to go dead so quickly.)

Once the dune buggy is assembled and the battery is charged, it’s a lot of fun for kids. The assembly is a chore for adults, though. I took almost an hour and a half to assemble. Most of that time was spent putting on the wheels. The directions aren’t clear and some of the screws are hard to get to and there isn’t room to use an electric screwdriver. As long as you allow enough time for assembly and charging the battery, this dune buggy will be a hit.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle Well, this was kind of educational, and it was kind of a frenetic, fun 15 minutes trying to put things back together, but the end comments were "This is ridiculous" and "Well they could have made that better." The ridiculous part was how they made decisions to cut the pieces. They do not follow international borders very faithfully and randomly cut larger countries into random parts. Pieces that include only one country do not resemble the country at all. the eastern united states is a irregular rectangle that appears to miss New England and average out Florida. France is a strange amporphous shape. Canada and Russia are random blotches of non interconnecting shapes.

I like the story that the first puzzle was a US map cut into pieces in a classroom to teach geography. This could have been similar except that the countries are so crudely hacked in shapes. But it does give an idea of location and cultural icons like the great wall of china, russian dolls, local animals are located on the map. I was very impressed that the Great Barrier Reef made the map as an entity. But it could have been so much better in the way it was handled.

As for how it was made, the pieces are small and found to be easy to misplace. The magnetism is weak but sufficient to keep the pieces loosely on the board. The backing is very flexible and all in all it does not seem to be a super well built product.
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA X1 4 Channel 2.4G Rc Quad Copter - UFO Durability
After many hit walls and a fall from 4 stories high, it is still going great. It is so light weight that it can take a fall, like an ant falling from a tree. The key is to throttle down before crashes.

Speed
On High mode it really tilts.

Range
The wireless range is excellent and the battery life is just fine. I've flown it at least a hundred feet away with no loss of a connection. So far I've been happy with the battery. Charges in 60 minutes and flies for 8.

Fun
Finding a good building to fly in is key. The building I work in has an open 4 story architecture with bridges at each level. The flip button is also fun for impressing on lookers.

Note
Plug the battery in when it is level so that the gyros are initialized correctly.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA X1 4 Channel 2.4G Rc Quad Copter - UFO
